{
  "thinking": "The round's just started and the pad is still blank, so nothing can be built until Leo drafts and locks a design. I want the table to pick an animal whose outline reads on its own, and I want the start placed where every line leaves the same way.",
  "say": "Morning, team. Before Leo sketches, can I push for a fish in side view? One closed outline, with the tail fin as its own telltale shape. Start at the back of the tail, run the top of the body forward to the head, split there, and bring both sides back round to the tail. Lines leaving the start all head the same way, so it should fall cleanly. Fins and eyes are separate bits that won't fall, so let's keep them out of the run.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 6,
  "point": [4, 10],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Round start, pad blank, Leo drafting. Proposed fish: start at tail base, top of body to head, split and return along belly to tail. Keep fins/eyes off the run (they won't fall). Review the draft once it appears: check start direction, joins, and that the tail fin reads."
}
